items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: P. Rohn is mentioned only as a name appearing on record credits ('Piku has his name on some of those too, P. Rohn') which the interviewee and Johnny Dodds were discussing.

ctx.x: I heard that song as a white religious piece.

Really? A religious group. The oldest record I ever came across was an old Paramount which wasn't anything very jazzy, you might say. a quartet. You know, a sacred quartet. But anyway, to get back to Dodds, I was surprised then, of course, that to me he was somebody famous. Anybody on the Louis Hot Five would be a famous musician. And he even had a sign out in the front. I was surprised that that was in the first big popularity cycle of Benny Goodman had just made his big hit out in California at the Palladium or…
